items.title: Scooby-Doo: Origins Reveals Cute New Photo of the Live-Action Dog
items.author: Jim Vejvoda
items.content:
Netflix announced Sunday that production has officially wrapped in Atlanta on their upcoming series Scooby-Doo: Origins. The streaming service also released a new photo of the titular good boy, which can be seen in the image gallery below.

Scooby-Doo: Origins marks the first time a real Great Dane has portrayed the beloved canine member of the Mystery Inc. gang.

“During their final summer at camp, old friends Shaggy and Daphne get embroiled in a haunting mystery surrounding a lonely lost Great Dane puppy that may have been a witness to a supernatural murder,” according to the official synopsis.

“Together with the pragmatic and scientific townie, Velma, and the strange, but ever so handsome new kid, Freddy, they set out to solve the case that is pulling each of them into a creepy nightmare that threatens to expose all of their secrets.”

Scooby-Doo: Origins stars Mckenna Grace as “Daphne Blake,” Tanner Hagen as “Shaggy Rogers,” Abby Ryder Fortson as “Velma Dinkley,” Maxwell Jenkins as “Fred Jones.”

Other cast members include Paul Walter Hauser, Rusty Schwimmer, Peter Macon, Jona Xiao, Dani Deetté, Elysée Sanvillé, Alex Isles, Avery Kristen Pohl, Pamela Mitchell, Ross Kimball, Sara Gilbert, Wynn Everett, Sauriyan Sapkota, Bruce McGill, André Benjamin, and Cathy Moriarity.

Josh Appelbaum and Scott Rosenberg serve as executive producers and showrunners.

Executive producers include Greg Berlanti, Sarah Schechter, Leigh London Redman (via Berlanti Productions and its overall deal with Warner Bros. Television), André Nemec, Jeff Pinkner, and Adrienne Erickson (via Midnight Radio), and Toby Haynes (EP/Episode 101 Director).

Scooby-Doo: Origins will launch globally in 2027.

items.title: StarCraft Devs Promise New Game Will Definitely Release in 2030
items.description: We got the chance to speak with the developers of the new StaCcraft game, who explained why they shared such a distant release date and even teased some potential gameplay elements.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
We got the chance to speak with the developers of the new StarCraft game, who explained why they shared such a distant release date and even teased some potential gameplay elements for this highly-anticipated title.

StarCraft is finally getting a new game, and it’s taking a drastically different approach from its predecessors; instead of an RTS, Blizzard’s grisly sci-fi property is making its debut in the realm of open-world shooters, and it’s set to launch in 2030.

That’s a long way out from now, and it’s anyone’s guess as to what the world will look like in four years. We got the chance to ask the developers everyone’s burning question at Blizzcon 2026: Why announce the game if there’s still so much time left before it releases?

Dan Hay, GM & VP of StarCraft and AnaLee Haertling, Associate Director, told us that sharing a firm release date helps keep them “honest” — and yes, 2030 is a firm release date.

“You walk a funny line, because it’s like, you wanna tease, and we wanna say, ‘Hey, this is where we wanna land,’” Hay explained. “The reason why I love a really good date, is because the reality is that it puts a target. It allows us to say to a team that that’s what we’re going for. It’s a rallying cry, and we’re focused on that. We wanna make sure we deliver something that is fun, something that is powerful, and something that allows you to explore. But I also like the idea that there’s a frame that keeps us honest. And it says, ‘2030, let’s go.’”

When asked if 2030 was a solid date, Hay confirmed that it is, indeed, “solid.”

"I like the idea that there's a frame that keeps us honest."

While Hay couldn’t tell us how long the game has been in development, he did share some insight into how hard the team is working to transform StarCraft into a world that feels like a living, breathing universe that’s both welcoming to new players and recognizable to longtime fans.

“I can’t tell you how long it’s been in development with the team, but I can tell you how long it’s been in development in my head, and it’s probably about 25 years,” he joked. “For us, I think what’s important is that we've gone out to find people who really love the brand. We’ve gone out to people who know the brand, who come back and really feel the love of the legacy. We’ve taken great pains and great care to make something that feels authentic, that when you walk through this world, you recognize it.

“It's a tricky thing. It’s a bit of a knife’s edge. You wanna build something that is welcoming and inviting to new players but you wanna make sure it feels real. That when you walk into a bar it feels like a bar from the original world. When you meet players and characters and you see them, they've got the weapons and the armor and it feels authentic and it feels real.”

Hay went on to drop a few subtle hints at what players can expect in this new game, saying that StarCraft will bring into sharp focus the rough edges of its world, along with the visceral feeling of being a soldier fighting against massive, deadly creatures.

“We wanna show that it’s rough tools out there, it's a difficult world, it's filled with warfare and different factions and different groups of people, and they don’t always get along, and we wanted to bring that to bear from the very beginning,” he told us.

“When you think about what StarCraft will allow you to do, and we thought about how we tell this story — this is the way to tell that story. To be boots on the ground, to be down in the muck and the dirt, and to feel the tension of it.

“There was something really powerful — and I have to be careful not to give too much away here — I remember seeing the first time that a Hydralisk was 10 feet tall, and it was basically snapping at me. And I’ve got a gun and I’ve got armor, and I’m feeling like I’m down in the dirt and I’m feeling the weight of it. Emily was just talking about the deployment of the barracks. What’s super powerful about it is the moment you drop down on the ground, your perspective changes. It doesn’t feel like you’re a god looking down at this and you’re detached. It feels like, ‘My God, I'm in the middle of this. Every decision matters. Everything I do feels like it has gravitas.’”

"Every decision matters. Everything I do feels like it has gravitas."

He also dove into why Blizzard chose to take StarCraft in such a wildly different direction, rather than staying with the series’ RTS roots — and in doing so, shed some light on a few possible key gameplay elements, one of which is using an enemy as a “tool” against another enemy.

“For us, when we think about the themes and we think about the opportunity for you to be on the battlefield and for you to go out and think about the vista, the opportunity to explore, and then to discover, and then to disrupt. It’s incredibly unique. And then when you think about the different factions that there are, we just wanted people to go out into these worlds and actually get a sense of what it’s like to meet these different groups.

“Again, I really wanna talk about this stuff, but I also have to hold some stuff back, but what's really important is you think about some of these different factions in StarCraft, and you think about what they bring and you think about the way that it feels. I have imagery in my head right now that I can be careful not to describe, but I’m seeing an awful lot of biomass, and I’m seeing a lot of stuff we were hinting at. If you look at the teaser and you start to see that moment where the barracks is flying in and you look at the planet, you’ll actually see all the things that are alive on that planet and get a sense of that feel.

“For us, it felt right to put you down on the ground in the middle of people that are fighting and they don’t agree. This feeling of, ‘The enemy of my enemy is a tool to be used.’ We felt like the open world and the opportunity to explore and to discover and of course to disrupt and to use my enemy against another enemy felt really powerful.”

StarCraft is still a ways out, but you can catch up on all the other exciting news Blizzard had to offer in our round-up blog for the event's Opening Ceremony and take a peek at everything that's available to play right now.

items.title: Overwatch Reveals First Look at New Omnic Hero Coming Later This Year
items.description: Blizzard has teased another new Overwatch Hero after revealing Doctrine just moments ago.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Blizzard has teased another new Overwatch Hero after revealing Doctrine just moments ago.

Just as fans of the long-running hero shooter took to social media to celebrate the reveal of Overwatch's new vampire-themed Support Hero, Blizzard snuck in another surprise with a post on its social media page. What seemed to be an innocent enough post showed off the full new Hero roster for 2026 – but wait, who's that?

Doctrine has joined Jetpack Cat, Anran, Emre, Dmon, Mizuki, Shion, Domina, and Sierra, but tucked in the far-right side of the group photo is a character no one has ever seen before. It turns out the image included a first look at a yet-to-be-named Omnic with a robotic trench coat, a swanky hat, and what seems to be an umbrella weapon. All we know for now is that he is Hero 55 and he's another Support, and fans, of course, are losing their minds at the nonchalant reveal.

HOLLLLYYYY pic.twitter.com/oY3VsaKfFE

— M1das (@M1das_OW2) September 12, 2026

"NEED THIS MYSTERIOUS SHERLOCK HOLMES OMNIC BADLY," one fan said.

"I just know his umbrella showers some healing droplets I just can't prove it," another fan theorized.

"NOW THAT IS A COOL HERO, OMNIC DETECTIVE WITH AN UMBRELLA WEAPON LETS GOOO," another added.

Blizzard has previously kept its cards close to its chest when it came to new Overwatch Hero reveals, mostly limiting designs to silhouettes, previously. For this unnamed Omnic and for BlizzCon 2026, it's made an exception. Many fans have also noted that the design we see here is far different from the one we were originally shown at the Spotlight presentation in February of this year, though it appears his general design has remained intact. It's a good thing, too, because fans already really like what they see, even if it's not quite what was expected.

so why he got a debuff? where is my omnic detective pic.twitter.com/0rIUiM2mAG

— R3medy (@iligy1) September 12, 2026

WHAT A BEAUTIFUL YEAR FOR NEW HEROES pic.twitter.com/6uRVUrbQtb

— Moira (@TransMoira) September 12, 2026

Overwatch was one of a few games to make a big splash at BlizzCon 2026. In addition to Doctrine, who will launch with Season 5 October 6, Dokiwatch is returning, with Blizzard also planning big reworks for Sombra and Roadhog. Game director Aaron Keller has also teased big things in store for the team's February 2027 spotlight, promising that they are "aiming for peak Overwatch."

For now, however, we'll have to wait to see where the Omnic Hero will fall on the roster and how he will shake up the meta. In the meantime, you can check out everything else announced during the BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony here.

items.title: Diablo 5 Forging the Next Era Panel: Everything Announced
items.description: Blizzard has revealed three classes for Diablo 5, a first look at its UI, and shown off even more as part of its Forging the Next Era panel at BlizzCon 2026.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Blizzard has revealed three classes for Diablo 5, a first look at its UI, and shown off even more as part of its Forging the Next Era panel at BlizzCon 2026.

The next Diablo game might be years away from its spring 2029 launch, but that didn't stop some members of the development team from confirming the first details. Highlights from the 45-minute panel include confirmation that the Demon Hunter and Monk are two returning classes, but a new class is coming too: the Plague Knight.

Concept art, gameplay details, and more were all revealed as part of the big panel presentation. Blizzard also talked about why it decided to make the announcement now, almost three years before launch. We gathered all of the highlights for newcomers and die-hard fans to comb through right here. You can see everything announced at the Diablo 5 BlizzCon panel below.

The Diablo Team Takes the Stage

Multiple members from the Diablo team have taken the stage at BlizzCon 2026. After the surprise reveal for Diablo 5, it's clear the developers have a lot to talk about. Shely said the plan is for the panel to cover the story, world, gameplay, and even some information about itemization.

"We're a long way from the campfire, from its comfort and hope. These are the fires of Diablo. Sanctuary has been destroyed, and Diablo has won," Shely said.

A New Dark Lord

Producer Matt Zitterman said, when deciding how to approach more Diablo, Blizzard first had to decide whether to do more DLC or another mainline entry. When looking at Diablo 4 and an opportunity to bring back the true Diablo, a proper sequel with Diablo 5 is the only thing that really made sense.

"Once we decided that this game was going to bring Diablo back, we knew we had to do it right," narrative director Jennifer Brandes Hpler said. "He couldn't just be a final boss. He needs to be a boss that's shaping this game from its opening moments. That's how we decided that, this time, you're not scrambling to shape Sanctuary before Diablo tries to take it over."

Shely added that Diablo "has a lot more to say" in this game. Don't expect Diablo to have some tragic backstory in Diablo 5, though.

"Pretty quickly we kept arriving at the same conclusion: Diablo is Diablo. He is the Lord of Terror," senior producer Tiffany Wat said. "He's not redeemable. He's not misunderstood. That gave us a lot of clarity, so the question now becomes not 'Is he right?' but 'What happens now that he's won?'"

Returning to Westmarch

Shely teased that returning to Westmarch will see players confronting a place that has become an "outpost of Hell." That means very few humans have not bowed to the Lord of Terror or become cultists, with some humans even turning to become Dread Commanders, which harness the power of the Dukes of Hell.

Blizzard also confirmed terrain will change when players return to certain areas. Procedural worlds are also coming back with Diablo 5.

"That idea of not knowing what's around the corner creates a lot of tension," Wat said. "So, in Diablo 5, we're bringing back the procedural world, both in the dungeons and the overworld. So, if you go back to a region that you've been before, all that information knew yesterday - that path that I found, that landmark that I was moving toward, how to fight those Elite monsters - none of that is information is going to help me today."

Diablo fans know Treasure Goblins to be "loot pinatas," but in Diablo 5, one character will change that. Wat teased Zarg, a new character and a Treasure Goblin that players will grow to know. His name's not final and neither are his character details, but he's yet another sign that Blizzard is shaking things up for its next big installment.

First Diablo 5 Classes Confirmed

Shely teased some of the classes coming to Diablo 5. The Demon Hunter and Monk are two returning classes coming to the game. New classes are coming, too, including the heavily armored Plague Knight, which will see players spreading disease and then consuming it for power. That's all he was willing to tease today, but he did say that Diablo 5 will launch with more classes than any other entry than ever before.

"I don't just mean just more classes than any Diablo game at ship," he elaborated. "I mean more classes total. The thing about Diablo classes is they're approachable - you can jump in and immediately have an exciting time playing them - but there's also deep ARPG mastery there and a multitude of builds to explore."

Itemization in Diablo 5

Diablo 5 is still very early in development, so how it handles itemization is still being put together. However, the team was willing to share a sneak peek at concept art for what things look like in this stage of work. Gear-based sets are coming back, with Shely also confirmed that there will be multi-slot items.

"I like to think of itemization kind of like a city," Shely said. "Think about New York City; It's an enormous metropolis, you can immediately go to Time Square and immediately find something cool. That's kind of how I think about our set up. Once you really start to dig in and master it, you learn where's the best deli, where's the best pizza, and you really get into that crunchy opportunity to define your own builds. That's what we want to do in D5."

This is more from Diablo 5 many likely expected to see, but Blizzard doesn't want fans to be overwhelmed by the image they see here. Shely teased that they've got some "really great solutions for any controller players who might be worried about manipulating those items."

Why Announce Diablo 5 Now?

All of the words shared by the Diablo team during the Forging the Next Era BlizzCon 2026 panel are all fine and good, but some fans may be worried that, with years to go until launch, there's no telling what the final product will look like. Zitterman promised that Diablo 5 is a game they hope to build alongside the community, which is why we're learning about it years before its planned launch.

"I think for us it's super important that Diablo 5 feels unmistakably Diablo, in particular for our longtime players," Zitterman said. "That starts with what I talked about at the beginning: Understanding who are Diablo players at their core? What do they want, what do they need, out of a Diablo game?"

He continued: "When you're building a game, you need other people to look at your work and give you that critical feedback. We want to get that feedback now. We want to get that feedback as early as possible. It's why we're announcing today. It's why we're excited to bring the community into the process of making the game along the way toward our launch date."

Zitterman signed off the news portion of the panel by telling players that they won't have to wait long for updates. The plan is for the team to share "regular updates about how development is going" starting in 2027.

"We talked about how D5 will let you define your identity, discover builds, chase memorable loot, right?" Shely added. "More than that, our job is to build the game players want - that you want. Not what we think you should want. We want to build the best Diablo game, and that means listening to you; listening to your feedback, and allowing it to shape the game."

Image courtesy of Blizzard Entertainment.

"That idea of not knowing what's around the corner creates a lot of tension," Wat said. "So, in Diablo 5, we're bringing back the procedural world, both in the dungeons and the overworld. So, if you go back to a region that you've been before, all that information knew yesterday - that path that I found, that landmark that I was moving toward, how to fight those Elite monsters - none of that is information is going to help me today."

Diablo fans know Treasure Goblins to be "loot pinatas," but in Diablo 5, one character will change that. Wat teased Zarg, a new character and a Treasure Goblin that players will grow to know. His name's not final and neither are his character details, but he's yet another sign that Blizzard is shaking things up for its next big installment.

First Diablo 5 Classes Confirmed

Shely teased some of the classes coming to Diablo 5. The Demon Hunter and Monk are two returning classes coming to the game. New classes are coming, too, including the heavily armored Plague Knight, which will see players spreading disease and then consuming it for power. That's all he was willing to tease today, but he did say that Diablo 5 will launch with more classes than any other entry than ever before.

"I don't just mean just more classes than any Diablo game at ship," he elaborated. "I mean more classes total. The thing about Diablo classes is they're approachable - you can jump in and immediately have an exciting time playing them - but there's also deep ARPG mastery there and a multitude of builds to explore."

Itemization in Diablo 5

Diablo 5 is still very early in development, so how it handles itemization is still being put together. However, the team was willing to share a sneak peek at concept art for what things look like in this stage of work. Gear-based sets are coming back, with Shely also confirmed that there will be multi-slot items.

"I like to think of itemization kind of like a city," Shely said. "Think about New York City; It's an enormous metropolis, you can immediately go to Time Square and immediately find something cool. That's kind of how I think about our set up. Once you really start to dig in and master it, you learn where's the best deli, where's the best pizza, and you really get into that crunchy opportunity to define your own builds. That's what we want to do in D5."

This is more from Diablo 5 many likely expected to see, but Blizzard doesn't want fans to be overwhelmed by the image they see here. Shely teased that they've got some "really great solutions for any controller players who might be worried about manipulating those items."

Why Announce Diablo 5 Now?

All of the words shared by the Diablo team during the Forging the Next Era BlizzCon 2026 panel are all fine and good, but some fans may be worried that, with years to go until launch, there's no telling what the final product will look like. Zitterman promised that Diablo 5 is a game they hope to build alongside the community, which is why we're learning about it years before its planned launch.

"I think for us it's super important that Diablo 5 feels unmistakably Diablo, in particular for our longtime players," Zitterman said. "That starts with what I talked about at the beginning: Understanding who are Diablo players at their core? What do they want, what do they need, out of a Diablo game?"

He continued: "When you're building a game, you need other people to look at your work and give you that critical feedback. We want to get that feedback now. We want to get that feedback as early as possible. It's why we're announcing today. It's why we're excited to bring the community into the process of making the game along the way toward our launch date."

Zitterman signed off the news portion of the panel by telling players that they won't have to wait long for updates. The plan is for the team to share "regular updates about how development is going" starting in 2027.

"We talked about how D5 will let you define your identity, discover builds, chase memorable loot, right?" Shely added. "More than that, our job is to build the game players want - that you want. Not what we think you should want. We want to build the best Diablo game, and that means listening to you; listening to your feedback, and allowing it to shape the game."

items.title: X-Men Star Inde Navarrette Teases Her Plan to Nail Rogue’s Southern Accent
items.description: Obsession breakout Inde Navarrette already has a plan to make sure she nails Rogue's iconic Southern accent in the new X-Men movie.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Obsession breakout Inde Navarrette already has a plan to make sure she nails Rogue's iconic Southern accent in the new X-Men movie.

Navarrette will jump from horror to the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) when she appears in X-Men in 2028. As revealed last month, it's due out May 5, 2028, but even more than Rogue's power-stealing abilities and fierce attitude, fans have been dying to know if Navarrette will bring any spice to Rogue's voice.

The character is known for her southern draw, especially thanks to the delivery made popular by original X-Men animated series voice actress Lenore Zann. Navarrette may not have the natural accent audiences would expect from Rogue, but she told Entertainment Tonight that the mutant team member's voice is very much already on her mind.

"I've never told this publicly – I completely forgot – but I have a divorced family. I grew up in Texas for a good majority of my life," Navarrette said when asked how she'll build Rogue's voice. "So, honestly, those Southern women are really my favorite."

Navarrette then noted her specific connection to Corpus Christi, a coastal town located toward the south end of Texas. For the Obsession actress-turned-Marvel superhero, it's the "old Southern women" that she "really, really loves." But her appreciation for the South doesn't stop there.

"But, specifically, Mississippi – Rogue is from Mississippi," she continued. "So, I really just want to go there. I wanna really do her justice."

Navarrette is just one piece of a grander MCU puzzle. Also confirmed for the big MCU X-Men reboot movie are Adam Driver as Mister Sinister, Maya Boyd as Storm, Christopher Abbott as Professor X, Sadie Sink as Jean Grey, Kit Connor as Cyclops, and Samara Weaving as Emma Frost. Gen V and Scream 7 star Asa Germann was also recently picked to play the winged mutant, Angel.

So many other pieces need to come together before X-Men arrives, but director Jake Schreier has teased a team-up movie worth waiting for. In August, he talked about some of the comic books he's looking to for inspiration, promising to give MCU fans a movie that is a "new spin" on what they've seen with past live-action X-Men films. Meanwhile, Navarrette is reportedly so excited to do the movie that she passed up a part in Heat 2.

Photo by Frazer Harrison/Getty Images.

items.title: Blizzard's Big BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony Mic Drop Is World of Warcraft Forever
items.description: Blizzard ended its BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony with the announcement of World of Warcraft Forever.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
Blizzard ended its BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony with the announcement of World of Warcraft Forever.

This “Classic Plus” MMO is developed by the World of Warcraft Classic team, and is set during the first year of World of Warcraft. It features three new zones, several overhauled existing zones, and over 1,000 quests. Elsewhere, there are nine new dungeons and even a new race.

Blizzard showed off a cinematic for World of Warcraft Forever during the Opening Ceremony, confirming a release date for November 4.

Also at BlizzCon, Blizzard announced the next content update for World of Warcraft: Midnight, called Eclipse. Fans were treated to a cinematic alongside a gameplay trailer, before the teaser fans had hoped for. The Last Titan, the final chapter of the Worldsoul Saga, is coming.

Here's everything announced at BlizzCon 2026 for more.

items.title: Diablo 5 Announced
items.description: Blizzard has officially announced Diablo 5 at BlizzCon 2026. Set entirely in a post-apocalyptic future 100 years after Diablo 4, the ARPG will release in 2029.
items.author: Michael Peyton
items.content:
Diablo 5, a brand-new mainline entry in Blizzard’s long-running action RPG series, was announced today at BlizzCon 2026.

A short teaser during today's BlizzCon opening ceremony shows the return of the Lord of Terror, one century after the events of Diablo 4.

The Diablo development team also revealed that Diablo 5 will release in Spring 2029, a full 6 years after the release of Diablo 4, and more than three decades after the series first launched.

Diablo 5’s story is confirmed to take place a full century after the events of Diablo 4, and will be the first game in the series that is set entirely post-apocalypse.

More about Diablo 5 was revealed later in the day when the development team took to the stage during the Diablo 5 Forging the Next Era Panel to dive deeper into the game.

BlizzCon 2026 also saw more Diablo news, including The Amazon - a new class pack coming to Diablo 4 in 2027, word that the Diablo 4 Collection coming to Nintendo Switch 2, and Season 15, a broad playable look-back at the history of the Diablo franchise, which is available now.

For more from BlizzCon 2026, check out everything announced.

items.title: Overwatch Gets New Vampire-Inspired Support Hero, Map, and Big Character Reworks
items.description: Overwatch is getting a brand-new vampire-inspired support hero, as well as the conclusion of Act III in The Reign of Talon storyline and several big character changes.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Overwatch is getting a brand-new vampire-inspired support hero, as well as the conclusion of Act III in The Reign of Talon storyline and several big character changes.

Our new addition is Doctrine, a vampire support hero who deals lots of damage and healing with a high mechanical floor. He comes with a brand-new playable escort map, Watch Point Grimsvotn, a volcanic prison where he’s being held captive. What’s more, he’ll be playable for a trial weekend starting today, September 12, both on the BlizzCon convention floor and at home.

In other big news, Overwatch Season 5 begins on October 6. Dokiwatch is also returning, and there are some major character reworks planned: Roadhog is being reworked into a tank that “actually helps his team,” per Blizzard franchise leaders, while Sombra is moving into the support class.

The Overwatch 2026 World Cup Finals are also taking place at BlizzCon this weekend, featuring live performances from Japanese pop group YOASOBI and K-Pop group LE SSERAFIM.

A new hero was also mentioned coming in Season 6, as well as a new Spotlight happening in February 2027, which will include a "new story, a fresh set of heroes, and amazing new systems" that the team said will bring the game back to "peak Overwatch."

Also taking place this weekend is a special event that Overwatch has never done before; at BlizzCon, the voice of Cole Cassidy, Matt Mercer, will be leading an Overwatch tabletop RPG session, leading the voice actors for Symmetra, Sombra, Reinhardt, and Vendetta in a one-of-a-kind story built especially for this convention. BlizzCon will also be auctioning off figures, merchandise, artwork, collectibles, and more to benefit Make-A-Wish.

We also have to mention Overwatch's collaboration with LE SSERAFIM, which is available now. This collab includes stylish themed cosmetics, emotes, and in-game challenges.

For more BlizzCon coverage, check out everything announced at the BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony.

items.title: Next StarCraft Game Announced at BlizzCon as an Open-World Shooter, but It’s Not Due Out Until 2030
items.description: It’s been over 15 years since Blizzard’s beloved real-time strategy game, StarCraft 2, came out. Now, a new game in the series has been announced — but it’s still years away.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
It’s been over 15 years since Blizzard’s beloved real-time strategy game, StarCraft 2, came out. Now, a new game in the series has been announced — but it’s still years away.

Revealed at BlizzCon 2026, the simply named StarCraft is the next title in the sci-fi franchise, and it’s going to look markedly different from its predecessors.

In fact, it’s a completely different genre. StarCraft is an open-world shooter, and it’s due out in 2030. While this distant launch window makes it hard to get too excited about StarCraft just yet, Blizzard has a history of announcing games far before they're ready for the public to play. In fact, it’s something the company behind Warcraft, Diablo, and Overwatch is notorious for doing, historically touting the mantra: “It’ll be ready when it’s ready.”

The announcement of a new StarCraft game was expected at BlizzCon, after the official StarCraft website became rife with visual ‘glitches,’ and issued a ‘warning’ telling users their device has been “compromised.” Fans took this to mean that a big update for the franchise was on the horizon, and they were right.

Indeed, rumors of a StarCraft shooter had been circling for years. In 2024, Bloomberg reporter Jason Schreier told IGN’s Podcast Unlocked about Blizzard’s third attempt at developing a StarCraft shooter with former Far Cry executive producer Dan Hay, who joined Blizzard in 2022, leading the charge. Then, later in 2024, a job posting was listed for an ‘upcoming open-world shooter’ that fans were certain was tied to this StarCraft game.

Blizzard has had a tough time developing StarCraft shooters over the years. StarCraft Ghost, announced in 2002, was going to be a tactical-action console game in which you played as a deadly Ghost operative in the employ of the Dominion, but it was canceled in 2006 after a series of delays.

A second attempt to make a StarCraft shooter, codenamed Ares, was canceled in 2019 so Blizzard could focus on Diablo 4 and Overwatch 2. Ares was reportedly “like Battlefield in the StarCraft universe,” but, like Ghost, fell by the wayside.

Now, it’s a case of third time lucky for Blizzard with this new StarCraft shooter in development. Check out everything announced at BlizzCon 2026 for all the news from across Blizzard.

items.title: Animated Diablo Show in the Works at Netflix
items.description: An animated Diablo show is in the works at Netflix, as announced at Blizzcon 2026, and there could be more to com
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
An animated Diablo show is in the works at Netflix, as announced at Blizzcon 2026, and there could be more to come.

Blizzard president Johanna Faries revealed the news, alongside a teaser for future series based on some of the company's other properties.

"We are thrilled to share that we are in development for a new animated series for Diablo with Netflix," she told the crowd. "As a big Diablo player myself, and someone who loves the indulgent darkness of Sanctuary, I am very excited to see this project come to life. It's just the beginning; to our Overwatch community, to our Warcraft community, and who knows — perhaps even some of our other universes, just know there are great discussions being had.

"And while I begged and pleaded to be able to share more, I can’t spill the beans just yet. I promise, as soon as we can, we will share more details with you."

We are thrilled to share that we are in development on a new animated series for Diablo with Netflix. pic.twitter.com/F7dKh73f12

— Diablo (@Diablo) September 12, 2026

"After decades of bringing entire universes to life through our games, we’re partnering with some creative powerhouses to tell even more stories beyond gaming across new screens," Blizzard said in a press release. "A new animated series set in the world of Diablo is in development with Netflix. More details will be shared in the future, but this is only the beginning, with even more taking shape across our universes."

A slew of other big reveals were announced for the franchise at Blizzcon, the biggest of which was the reveal of Diablo 5, set to release in Spring 2029. This game takes place after Sanctuary has fallen, where our big bad, Diablo himself, has won.

"For the first time, you won't be fighting to stop Diablo for taking Sanctuary. You'll enter a world where he already has. There are no towns or safe places to protect you. ...what must you become when the world has already fallen?" Blizzard franchise leaders said during the Saturday showcase.

A new class pack, the Amazon, is also coming to Diablo 4 in 2027. The Diablo 4 collection is coming to Nintendo Switch 2, and Season 15 is available now, giving players a look back at the entire history of the Diablo series.

items.title: Heroes of the Storm Gets First New Character in Six Years
items.description: Announced at Blizzcon 2026, Heroes of the Storm is getting its first new character since Hogger was released in 2020, as well as a new PTR.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Blizzard’s flagship MOBA, Heroes of the Storm, is finally showing signs of life.

Announced at Blizzcon 2026, the game is getting its first new character since Hogger was released in 2020, as well as a new PTR.

Xal'atath, the primary antagonist of World of Warcraft’s Midnight expansion, is coming to the Nexus on Monday, September 28. The PTR begins on Monday, September 14.

This is a welcome surprise for Heroes of the Storm fans, who had all but accepted that the game might never get updated again. Blizzard ended official support for HotS in 2022, explaining that “future patches will primarily focus on client sustainability and bug fixing, with balance updates coming as needed."

However, the title received a significant patch in 2023, with smaller, sporadic changes and new skins trickling through in the years since then. Fans are more hopeful than ever, and Blizzard is, too — but future updates all depend on how the community responds to this fresh breath of air.

Speaking to the media, a Blizzard franchise leader said the company will “see how this does,” revealing that “if the community responds well, it could lead to more things” and describing this update as the "first foray into something really big.”

Blizzard President Johanna Faries thanked Heroes of the Storm players for holding out hope for so long, and even teased the addition of another new hero in the future.

"To all the HotS players out there, thank you for believing in this game, for carrying the torch, and for reminding us sometimes — very loudly — what this game means to you," she said. "And who knows — we might even have another new hero on the way in the future, so stay tuned, and we will see you in the Nexus."

"And who knows — we might even have another new hero on the way in the future, so stay tuned, and we will see you in the Nexus."

items.title: Borderlands 4 DLC Character and Free-to-Play Weekend Attract Resurgence on Steam
items.description: Borderlands 4 is climbing Steam charts as players fall head over heels for its new DLC character – a Vault Hunter named Loveless the Hacker.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Borderlands 4 is climbing Steam charts as players fall head over heels for its new DLC character – a Vault Hunter named Loveless the Hacker.

Gearbox Software's latest Borderlands game struggled in the months following its September 2025 launch. Despite delivering the looter shooter series' biggest launch ever, technical issues across PC and console, as well as Gearbox's handling of the situation, were immediately followed by a steep decline in players, with SteamDB recording numbers that have struggled to break 10,000 concurrent users since January of this year.

Borderlands 4 might have launched to generally favorable reviews (IGN gave it an 8/10), but it's struggled to recapture player interest – until now. Thursday, September 10, saw the release of Loveless the Hacker, a DLC character with high-end cybernetics. She's only a small part of a grander Story Pack 2 release, and she seems to be giving the game a second wind.

"Two minds exist inside Loveless, forming a synchronized set of lethal skills that strike as one," a description for Loveless says. "Through a symbiotic melding of the biological and digital, this ex-Anshin hacker-turned-assassin has become a superior lifeform. Equipped with the highest-end cybernetics, Loveless shares her psyche with a digital virus of her own creation, which can digistruct into a physical Wyrm form to act as a deadly extension of her shared, perfection-seeking will."

At the time of this story's publication, Borderlands 4 is enjoying around 26,000 concurrent players on Steam alone. That's the most it's had since November 2025, and far higher than the 17,000-player peak it reached with the launch of Story Pack 1 in March. The base game has also now managed to round out the Top 5 sellers on Steam in the U.S., and it's even come in at nine in the Top 10 global list.

Player counts also appear to be climbing even further, with those in its Steam reviews section specifically calling attention to Loveless as the reason they've decided to return to the planet Kairos. Many refer to voice acting from actress Carin Gilfry as a specific positive, but you can probably guess what a lot of the others had to say.

"Bought the game solely because of Loveless," one review said. "This is how you market."

Bro she’s so bad

Loveless? But girl I LOVE YOU pic.twitter.com/ASqXkrZhhX

— Ccrypto (@Ccrypto5) September 3, 2026

"Actually a nice character," a popular review said. "Looks good, good design, is insanely OP (can solo bosses without any help). But her alternate heads are a bit -- meh. And she costs $9.99. The VA put some effort into it though. Overall – I think she fits."

"Letting me buy the Vault Hunter without having to by the DLC story pack is the correct call," another fan said, referencing Loveless' $10 asking price compared to the recently released Story Pack 2 expansion. "Glad they learned. Also, step on me Mommy."

There are a number of factors contributing to Borderlands 4's boost in players on Steam, specifically. In addition to Loveless' status as a popular addition, Story Pack 2: FL4K and the Last Resort has also helped. There's also the fact that Gearbox is in the middle of a 50% off sale, bringing its price to $34.99 in the midst of a free-to-play weekend that runs until September 14.

It's unclear if the numbers will stick, but it seems to be a winning weekend for Borderlands 4 nonetheless. For more, you can read about what parent company Take-Two had to say about Gearbox's latest as it heads into its second year on the market. You can also read about how Saber took a dig at Gearbox CEO Randy Pitchford.

items.title: Level-5 Boss Addresses AI Backlash After Fans Hit Out at Game Reveal Showcase
items.description: Developer Level-5 has apologized for and explained its use of generative AI after fans spotted 'AI slop' in footage of games like Professor Layton and the Curious Village, DecaPolice, and more.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Developer Level-5 has apologized for and explained its use of generative AI after fans spotted "AI slop" in footage of games like Professor Layton and the Curious Village, DecaPolice, and more.

Concerns emerged following the studio's Nintendo Direct-style presentation earlier this week. Dubbed Level5 Vision 2026 II: Dreams, the show came with first looks at upcoming games, and it also happened to feature what fans suspected to be multiple examples of genAI.

Those who tuned into the 50-minute presentation spent more time talking about what they believed was evidence of AI use rather than the games, such as the Professor Layton remake, Yo-Kai Watch 2: Haunted Domain, and DecaPolice. The footage causing a stir is mostly limited to background scenes, but it's the fact that fans had to question Level-5 in the first place that's turned the situation into a full-fledged controversy for the Japan-based studio.

Oh no Level-5 is DEFINATELY using Gen AI to "update" Professor Layton. Especially when you compare the original backgrounds to the new. So many weird details and inconsistencies were added. https://t.co/AjVNfgetkk pic.twitter.com/0tRQ9vKn03

— AmericanYoshi (@AmericanYoshi) September 10, 2026

⁉️ Dans le nouveau trailer de Yo-kai Watch 2 : Haunted Domain, Nathan a… changé de visage ?! 😭#YOKAIWATCH
Hier (gauche) / Aujourd’hui (droite) pic.twitter.com/Vr3rzwNPA7

— Yo-net Watch (@YonetWatch) September 10, 2026

"I was SO excited when Level-5 announced their big comeback with Professor Layton, Decapolice, Yo-Kai Watch, and more," one fan on X/Twitter said. "But seeing this much blatant genAI being used across their games… yeah, this ain’t it"

"You were a beautiful studio," another fan said. "Now you are nothing more than a disappointment to us. We don’t want this AI s**t."

Level-5 president and CEO Akihiro Hino, who also hosted the showcase with his own animated avatar, took to X/Twitter to calm the noise. His message was both an apology and an explanation, confirming that Level-5 did, in fact, use generative AI for some aspects of development.

Hino described Level-5's heavy use of AI as "experimentation with the latest technology," adding that the team "sincerely apologizes to anyone who found this off-putting."

I was excited about Decapolice but Level-5 AI use is disgusting to me. I can't support that. https://t.co/EpxgBtCnDo

— Kabi (@KabiPlays) September 10, 2026

"However, please be assured that all elements defining the appeal and individuality of our released titles— such as the scenario, character designs, and foundational settings — are created entirely by human hands," Hino said (via Google translate). "We utilize AI primarily to streamline the process of digitizing human-created assets; for instance, accurately converting original artwork into 3D polygon models. You can rest assured that the games we release do not contain content simply generated by AI."

Hino also defended how Level-5 has used AI so far, saying: "the time saved through AI-driven efficiencies has allowed our creators to dedicate more of their efforts to the true essence of creativity." For him and the rest of the team, the belief is that the finished versions of games like Professor Layton and the Curious Village will still please fans in the end. Part of the reason it leaned so heavily on genAI this time around was so it could shrink "the development cycle for major titles from the current five years down to two."

"That said, we cannot deny that we made extensive use of AI this time, driven by a desire to deliver a presentation that was visually striking and easy to grasp," he continued. "We will take this experience as a learning opportunity for the future, so please look forward to Level-5’s next presentation."

pic.twitter.com/cict4COGTP

— ⬡ Nectur Bee ⬢ (@NecturBee) September 12, 2026

It's an explanation that hasn't gone over well in the Level-5 community. Replies to the post include fans still concerned about generative technology being used during development at all, fearing that affected games will be forever tarnished.

"Generative AI is trained on the stolen works of countless artists by tech companies to profit off their work, with the intent of replacing artists," one popular reply said. "By using it you replaced artists. You're profiting off of the skill of artists whose work has been stolen to power this software."

"I believe the human heart matters more than speed to market; surely it is better to take five years without using AI," another post written in Japanese said (via Google Translate). "If even a single asset is created using AI, the nagging worry — 'Is this image, piece of music, or line of dialogue made by AI or a human?' — would never go away. Isn't preserving that trust the most important thing?"

Hino didn't offer a specific game plan when it comes to how Level-5 will tweak its development plans going forward. For now, Professor Layton and the Curious Village, a remake of the original 2007 game, is slated to come to PC and consoles in 2027. Another new game in the series, the New World of Steam, is due out this December.

items.title: BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony: Everything Announced
items.description: BlizzCon 2026 is upon is, and IGN is reporting live on all the announcements direct from the opening ceremony. Expect big news on everything from World of Warcraft to Diablo, amid strong rumors of a StarCraft announcement.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony is over, and it did not disappoint, with huge announcements for StarCraft, Diablo, and Warcraft.

Highlights include the confirmation of StarCraft, an open-world shooter due out in... 2030! Before then, in 2029, we'll get Diablo 5. We also got the shadow-drop of a brand new campaign for Warcraft 3, and the announcement of World of Warcraft: Forever, due out in November.

Elsewhere, we have confirmation of a Diablo animated show for Netflix, a new hero for Overwatch, and a surprise new hero for Heroes of the Storm. Yep, there was a lot packed into Opening Ceremony, which will be followed by various panels that go into more detail on all the announcements.

In case you missed it, check out all the announcements in our live blog, below.

More from BlizzCon 2026

  • Diablo 5 Announced
  • Next StarCraft Game Announced at BlizzCon as an Open-World Shooter, but It’s Not Due Out Until 2030
  • Animated Diablo Show in the Works at Netflix
  • Blizzard's Big BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony Mic Drop Is World of Warcraft Forever
  • Overwatch 2 Gets New Vampire-Inspired Support Hero, Map, and Big Character Reworks
  • Blizzard Shadow-Drops New Campaign for Warcraft 3 at BlizzCon 2026
  • Heroes of the Storm Gets First New Character in Six Years

That's a wrap!

Holly Longdale brought BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony to a close by running through the big announcements and hyping up the crowd. It was certainly a news heavy Blizzcon - perhaps the biggest for future game reveals ever. Diablo 5 and the Warcraft 3 campaign certainly came as a huge shock. We all knew the StarCraft shooter was going to make an appearance due to various leaks, but it was still exciting to see the trailer. And how about World of Warcraft: Forever?

Let us know what you thought of Blizzcon 2026 Opening Ceremony in the comments, and stick with IGN for even more news from the event.

World of Warcraft: Forever announcement closes out BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony

Blizzard brought BlizzCon 2026's Opening Ceremony to an end with the announcement of World of Warcraft: Forever, which launches November 4, 2026. The beta starts this Thursday. Longdale called it "Classic Plus," on-stage.

World of Warcraft: forever "is your new permanent home," and "never ends," Longdale said. This is another way to play WoW that's "friendly, familiar, and new," and will live alongside modern and classic. The world is the "main character." Instead of one big heroic story, you carve your own path. It's also dedicated to community. There's no rush here: "it's the journey that counts, not the destination."

Forever is easy to get into and play but deep enough to play forever, Longdale added. It gets back to the heart of MMOs and what makes them so special.

Carve A New Path In A Legendary World.

WoW: Forever launches on November 4, 2026. pic.twitter.com/XYKHGwonFv

— World of Warcraft (@Warcraft) September 12, 2026

There new zones, new dungeons, new raids (10 and 20 players), new skills and talents, a new race (Skyborne) and class combinations, a new battleground, and over 1,000 new quests. There's even an SD/HD visuals toggle and a graphical overhaul.

In terms of the timeline and setting, this is Year 1 of Vanilla WoW, but the future is "untold." It sounds to me a bit like a soft reboot. Players will level up to 60 and stay at 60 indefinitely. "We don't want to race ahead and leave our accomplishments, our gear, and our friends behind," Longdale said. But there will be content updates.

WoW: Forever launches November 4 with:
⛓️ New dungeons
👨‍👨‍👦‍👦 10 & 20-player raids
🪽 Skyborne playable race
🗺️ New & expanded zones
✅ Account-wide perks
💡 Updated world visuals & lighting
🧟 New race & class combos
❗ 1000+ new quests

Join the Beta September 17! pic.twitter.com/hu4O0RpVtV

— World of Warcraft (@Warcraft) September 12, 2026

Warcraft 3 Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom announced

Warcraft 3 is back! Blizzard made the shock announcement of Warcraft 3's first new campaign in over 20 years, called Warcraft 3 Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom. And it's out... today!

Raise your banners: Warcraft III's first new campaign in over 20 years is here.

Return to the fields of war in Warcraft III Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom. 💀

AVAILABLE TODAY! pic.twitter.com/Y3M9NlBeQq

— World of Warcraft (@Warcraft) September 12, 2026

You experience the fall of Lordaeron and how it came to be the Undercity. This new prologue depicts the last days of Lordaeron, with over 30 hours of gameplay. A new Definitive Edition graphics mode is also in Reforged alongside a new neutral hero, the Forsaken Paladin. We got a gameplay trailer showing how it all looks.

Experience the fall of Lordaeron and the rise of the Forsaken ⚔️

With 30+ hours of new campaign content, Warcraft III Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom launches TODAY. pic.twitter.com/LVvgYyRGRg

— World of Warcraft (@Warcraft) September 12, 2026

World of Warcraft: The Last Titan

Hazzikostas teased the next World of Warcraft expansion, The Last Titan, which he said Blizzard couldn't talk about in detail because it would spoil the events of Midnight. But he did say it will "lay the groundwork for what comes next." Blizzard will reveal more early next year, but we did get a glimpse of what players will be up against via a new cinematic (it's big!). The Last Titan is due out in 2027.

Holly Longdale returned to the stage to declare: "We are putting the war back in Warcraft!"

The snow-packed peaks of Northrend cower below the spreading shadow of a singular and thundering judgment.

The conclusion to the Worldsoul Saga comes with World of Warcraft: The Last Titan. pic.twitter.com/iQSu8IUgs0

— World of Warcraft (@Warcraft) September 12, 2026

World of Warcraft: Midnight update

Holly Longdale, Vice President & Executive Producer, World of Warcraft, took to the stafe in a beautiful Warcraft-themed outfit to talk about the future of Warcraft. Longdale introduced Ian Hazzikostas, who talked about the Worldsoul Saga, Blizzard's trilogy of World of Warcraft expansions. Hazzikostas said World of Warcraft is at the mid-point of the Worldsoul Saga, with the second expansion, Midnight, half a year old. The next major content update for Midnight is called Eclipse, aka Patch 12.2.

Midnight falls as the Void breaches the heart of Azeroth.

There is no recourse; either face the darkness or be devoured:
🔮 Face Xal'atath
⛓️ Master a new dungeon & raid
🗡️ Claim a Legendary dagger
🌒 Journey into the very heart of our world pic.twitter.com/mcT5Jv5Syt

— World of Warcraft (@Warcraft) September 12, 2026

Hearthstone

Warcraft card game Hearthstone follows the Diablo 5 announcement with a "pretty epic expansion!" called Black Empire, due out October 20. Blizzard ran through a number of card reveals, and confirmed it's finally putting a narrative into the game. The updated journal launches alongside the Black Empire expansion. 2v2 Hearthstone is coming to the game for the first time, too. But the big news here is the Monk class is coming to Hearthstone in 2027. Expect more on Monk next year.

🐼 🙌 Why do we fight? To just have fun!

The new Monk class arrives next year, so keep an eye out for more details as we get closer to release! pic.twitter.com/HBLtm72T1S

— Hearthstone (@PlayHearthstone) September 12, 2026

Diablo 5 announced!

Blizzard shocked the BlizzCon crowd with the announcement of Diablo 5. We got the debut cinematic, which revolves around the return of The Lord of Terror himself, Diablo, to Sanctuary. "Sanctuary falls," is the tagline. It's out 2029. You enter a world in which Diablo has already won, with no towns or safe places waiting to protect players. "What must you become when the world has already fallen?" is the central question of Diablo 5. Expect more from a Diablo 5 panel later today.

I certainly wasn't expecting a Diablo 5 announcement at Blizzcon, but of course it makes sense that Blizzard is working on a sequel given how successful Diablo 4 has been and continues to be. Diablo 4 launched in June 2023, so Diablo 5 is due to arrive six years later.

Diablo 4 Nintendo Switch 2 and content updates announced

BlizzCon continued with a fun Diablo compilation video narrated by Deckard Cain himself.

Thirty years of putting you through Hell and you keep coming back for more. 😈

Here’s to the 30 years of Diablo and the best community alive. For now. pic.twitter.com/ZK9Aab7urd

— Diablo (@Diablo) September 12, 2026

Speaking of Deckard Cain, he leads Diablo 4 players through Season of Hell's Legacy, which sounds like a sort of demonic trip down memory lane in which you fight famous Diablo bosses. It launches on September 15. We also got the announcement of Diablo 4 coming to Nintendo Switch 2 alongside Season of Hell's Legacy.

Also in Diablo news, Spawn - yes, Spawn! - comes to mobile game Diablo Immortal on September 29.

In further Diablo 4 news, the Amazon class is finally coming to the game. She uses a bow and a javeline, and hits the game in the first half of 2027. Expect more from the Diablo 4 What's Next? panel at BlizzCon later this weekend.

Disciplined. Deadly. Legendary.

Built on the pillars of an expert soldier, unrivaled athleticism, and mythical magic, the Amazon enters Diablo IV as a new Class Pack in the first half of 2027 🏹 pic.twitter.com/vOmKzu1ChH

— Diablo (@Diablo) September 12, 2026

Overwatch new hero announced

Aaron Keller from the Overwatch team followed that big StarCraft reveal to talk Overwatch. Doctrine is a vampire support hero who uses bat drones to heal teammates and speed up their attacks. He's coming next month in Season 5, but his limited time Hero Trial kicks off right now and runs until September 14. Expect more information during a BlizzCon panel later this weekend.

Blizzard added that Overwatch Spotlight 2027 will kick off the next chapter in Overwatch's story.

StarCraft open-world shooter announced

Dan Hay, who used to work on Far Cry at Ubisoft, took to the BlizzCon stage to announce the heavily-rumored StarCraft first-person shooter. It's open-world, he confirmed, before declaring: "We are here to reignite this universe... and let's be honest... it's about damn time."

The game's debut cinematic showed Terran Dominion soldiers in training before a battle with the Zerg, which does not go well for our poor recruits. The game is simply titled StarCraft, and it's due out... in 2030! Only a four-year wait then, assuming it's not delayed. We didn't get a look at gameplay, and there are no details at all really other than it's open-world. Given Hay's background with Far Cry, I'm guessing StarCraft will work along the same lines.

So, it's not StarCraft 3, but it is more StarCraft! We've got so many questions. Hopefully BlizzCon answers them.

Diablo Netflix animated series

Blizzard announced a new animated series for Diablo on Netflix. Faries also teased Overwatch, Warcraft, and "who knows, perhaps even some of our other universes," are set for adaptations. "I promise, as soon as I can, we will share more details with you.

We are thrilled to share that we are in development on a new animated series for Diablo with Netflix. pic.twitter.com/F7dKh73f12

— Diablo (@Diablo) September 12, 2026

Heroes of the Storm gets a new character

Blizzard's MOBA, Heroes of the Storm, is coming back in a big way with a new character, Xal'atah, later this month, and another new character is coming at some point afterwards. "Thank you for believing in this game," Faries said. "For carrying that torch. Who knows? We might even have another new hero on the way in the near future. So stay tuned, and we will see you in the Nexus."

BlizzCon 2026 kicks off with flashy cinematic running through all the big games

BlizzCon 2026 has started with a rousing cinematic that runs through all the big hitters. Johanna Faries is on-stage to call it a "special moment for all of us." This is Faries' first BlizzCon as boss of Blizzard, and it sounds like she's close to tears as she praises and thanks her staff. "There's so much going on at Blizzard right now that we couldn't even fit it into this weekend if we tried," she said, perhaps teasing further unnanounced projects.

Five minutes to go!

BlizzCon 2026 starts in five minutes. We're expecting Johanna Faries, President of Blizzard Entertainment, on-stage soon to start the Opening Ceremony. Almost there!

We're taking our seats... and some photos!

With Opening Ceremony now just 30 minutes from kick-off, excitement is building inside Hall D at the Anaheim Convention Center. We're taking our seats now so we can report live from Blizzard's big showcase event. Check out these photos!

BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony is over, and it did not disappoint, with huge announcements for StarCraft, Diablo, and Warcraft.

Highlights include the confirmation of StarCraft, an open-world shooter due out in... 2030! Before then, in 2029, we'll get Diablo 5. We also got the shadow-drop of a brand new campaign for Warcraft 3, and the announcement of World of Warcraft: Forever, due out in November.

Elsewhere, we have confirmation of a Diablo animated show for Netflix, a new hero for Overwatch, and a surprise new hero for Heroes of the Storm. Yep, there was a lot packed into Opening Ceremony, which will be followed by various panels that go into more detail on all the announcements.

In case you missed it, check out all the announcements in our live blog, below.

More from BlizzCon 2026

  • Diablo 5 Announced
  • Next StarCraft Game Announced at BlizzCon as an Open-World Shooter, but It’s Not Due Out Until 2030
  • Animated Diablo Show in the Works at Netflix
  • Blizzard's Big BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony Mic Drop Is World of Warcraft Forever
  • Overwatch 2 Gets New Vampire-Inspired Support Hero, Map, and Big Character Reworks
  • Blizzard Shadow-Drops New Campaign for Warcraft 3 at BlizzCon 2026
  • Heroes of the Storm Gets First New Character in Six Years

That's a wrap!

Holly Longdale brought BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony to a close by running through the big announcements and hyping up the crowd. It was certainly a news heavy Blizzcon - perhaps the biggest for future game reveals ever. Diablo 5 and the Warcraft 3 campaign certainly came as a huge shock. We all knew the StarCraft shooter was going to make an appearance due to various leaks, but it was still exciting to see the trailer. And how about World of Warcraft: Forever?

Let us know what you thought of Blizzcon 2026 Opening Ceremony in the comments, and stick with IGN for even more news from the event.

World of Warcraft: Forever announcement closes out BlizzCon 2026 Opening Ceremony

Blizzard brought BlizzCon 2026's Opening Ceremony to an end with the announcement of World of Warcraft: Forever, which launches November 4, 2026. The beta starts this Thursday. Longdale called it "Classic Plus," on-stage.

World of Warcraft: forever "is your new permanent home," and "never ends," Longdale said. This is another way to play WoW that's "friendly, familiar, and new," and will live alongside modern and classic. The world is the "main character." Instead of one big heroic story, you carve your own path. It's also dedicated to community. There's no rush here: "it's the journey that counts, not the destination."

Forever is easy to get into and play but deep enough to play forever, Longdale added. It gets back to the heart of MMOs and what makes them so special.

Carve A New Path In A Legendary World.

WoW: Forever launches on November 4, 2026. pic.twitter.com/XYKHGwonFv

— World of Warcraft (@Warcraft) September 12, 2026

In terms of the timeline and setting, this is Year 1 of Vanilla WoW, but the future is "untold." It sounds to me a bit like a soft reboot. Players will level up to 60 and stay at 60 indefinitely. "We don't want to race ahead and leave our accomplishments, our gear, and our friends behind," Longdale said. But there will be content updates.

WoW: Forever launches November 4 with:
⛓️ New dungeons
👨‍👨‍👦‍👦 10 & 20-player raids
🪽 Skyborne playable race
🗺️ New & expanded zones
✅ Account-wide perks
💡 Updated world visuals & lighting
🧟 New race & class combos
❗ 1000+ new quests

Join the Beta September 17! pic.twitter.com/hu4O0RpVtV

— World of Warcraft (@Warcraft) September 12, 2026

Warcraft 3 Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom announced

Warcraft 3 is back! Blizzard made the shock announcement of Warcraft 3's first new campaign in over 20 years, called Warcraft 3 Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom. And it's out... today!

Raise your banners: Warcraft III's first new campaign in over 20 years is here.

Return to the fields of war in Warcraft III Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom. 💀

AVAILABLE TODAY! pic.twitter.com/Y3M9NlBeQq

— World of Warcraft (@Warcraft) September 12, 2026

You experience the fall of Lordaeron and how it came to be the Undercity. This new prologue depicts the last days of Lordaeron, with over 30 hours of gameplay. A new Definitive Edition graphics mode is also in Reforged alongside a new neutral hero, the Forsaken Paladin. We got a gameplay trailer showing how it all looks.

Experience the fall of Lordaeron and the rise of the Forsaken ⚔️

With 30+ hours of new campaign content, Warcraft III Reforged: Forsaken Kingdom launches TODAY. pic.twitter.com/LVvgYyRGRg

— World of Warcraft (@Warcraft) September 12, 2026

World of Warcraft: The Last Titan

Hazzikostas teased the next World of Warcraft expansion, The Last Titan, which he said Blizzard couldn't talk about in detail because it would spoil the events of Midnight. But he did say it will "lay the groundwork for what comes next." Blizzard will reveal more early next year, but we did get a glimpse of what players will be up against via a new cinematic (it's big!). The Last Titan is due out in 2027.

Holly Longdale returned to the stage to declare: "We are putting the war back in Warcraft!"

The snow-packed peaks of Northrend cower below the spreading shadow of a singular and thundering judgment.

The conclusion to the Worldsoul Saga comes with World of Warcraft: The Last Titan. pic.twitter.com/iQSu8IUgs0

— World of Warcraft (@Warcraft) September 12, 2026

World of Warcraft: Midnight update

Holly Longdale, Vice President & Executive Producer, World of Warcraft, took to the stafe in a beautiful Warcraft-themed outfit to talk about the future of Warcraft. Longdale introduced Ian Hazzikostas, who talked about the Worldsoul Saga, Blizzard's trilogy of World of Warcraft expansions. Hazzikostas said World of Warcraft is at the mid-point of the Worldsoul Saga, with the second expansion, Midnight, half a year old. The next major content update for Midnight is called Eclipse, aka Patch 12.2.

Midnight falls as the Void breaches the heart of Azeroth.

There is no recourse; either face the darkness or be devoured:
🔮 Face Xal'atath
⛓️ Master a new dungeon & raid
🗡️ Claim a Legendary dagger
🌒 Journey into the very heart of our world pic.twitter.com/mcT5Jv5Syt

— World of Warcraft (@Warcraft) September 12, 2026

Hearthstone

Warcraft card game Hearthstone follows the Diablo 5 announcement with a "pretty epic expansion!" called Black Empire, due out October 20. Blizzard ran through a number of card reveals, and confirmed it's finally putting a narrative into the game. The updated journal launches alongside the Black Empire expansion. 2v2 Hearthstone is coming to the game for the first time, too. But the big news here is the Monk class is coming to Hearthstone in 2027. Expect more on Monk next year.

🐼 🙌 Why do we fight? To just have fun!

The new Monk class arrives next year, so keep an eye out for more details as we get closer to release! pic.twitter.com/HBLtm72T1S

— Hearthstone (@PlayHearthstone) September 12, 2026

Diablo 5 announced!

Blizzard shocked the BlizzCon crowd with the announcement of Diablo 5. We got the debut cinematic, which revolves around the return of The Lord of Terror himself, Diablo, to Sanctuary. "Sanctuary falls," is the tagline. It's out 2029. You enter a world in which Diablo has already won, with no towns or safe places waiting to protect players. "What must you become when the world has already fallen?" is the central question of Diablo 5. Expect more from a Diablo 5 panel later today.

I certainly wasn't expecting a Diablo 5 announcement at Blizzcon, but of course it makes sense that Blizzard is working on a sequel given how successful Diablo 4 has been and continues to be. Diablo 4 launched in June 2023, so Diablo 5 is due to arrive six years later.

Diablo 4 Nintendo Switch 2 and content updates announced

BlizzCon continued with a fun Diablo compilation video narrated by Deckard Cain himself.

Thirty years of putting you through Hell and you keep coming back for more. 😈

Here’s to the 30 years of Diablo and the best community alive. For now. pic.twitter.com/ZK9Aab7urd

— Diablo (@Diablo) September 12, 2026

Speaking of Deckard Cain, he leads Diablo 4 players through Season of Hell's Legacy, which sounds like a sort of demonic trip down memory lane in which you fight famous Diablo bosses. It launches on September 15. We also got the announcement of Diablo 4 coming to Nintendo Switch 2 alongside Season of Hell's Legacy.

Also in Diablo news, Spawn - yes, Spawn! - comes to mobile game Diablo Immortal on September 29.

Disciplined. Deadly. Legendary.

Built on the pillars of an expert soldier, unrivaled athleticism, and mythical magic, the Amazon enters Diablo IV as a new Class Pack in the first half of 2027 🏹 pic.twitter.com/vOmKzu1ChH

— Diablo (@Diablo) September 12, 2026

Overwatch new hero announced

Aaron Keller from the Overwatch team followed that big StarCraft reveal to talk Overwatch. Doctrine is a vampire support hero who uses bat drones to heal teammates and speed up their attacks. He's coming next month in Season 5, but his limited time Hero Trial kicks off right now and runs until September 14. Expect more information during a BlizzCon panel later this weekend.

Blizzard added that Overwatch Spotlight 2027 will kick off the next chapter in Overwatch's story.

StarCraft open-world shooter announced

Dan Hay, who used to work on Far Cry at Ubisoft, took to the BlizzCon stage to announce the heavily-rumored StarCraft first-person shooter. It's open-world, he confirmed, before declaring: "We are here to reignite this universe... and let's be honest... it's about damn time."

The game's debut cinematic showed Terran Dominion soldiers in training before a battle with the Zerg, which does not go well for our poor recruits. The game is simply titled StarCraft, and it's due out... in 2030! Only a four-year wait then, assuming it's not delayed. We didn't get a look at gameplay, and there are no details at all really other than it's open-world. Given Hay's background with Far Cry, I'm guessing StarCraft will work along the same lines.

So, it's not StarCraft 3, but it is more StarCraft! We've got so many questions. Hopefully BlizzCon answers them.

Diablo Netflix animated series

Blizzard announced a new animated series for Diablo on Netflix. Faries also teased Overwatch, Warcraft, and "who knows, perhaps even some of our other universes," are set for adaptations. "I promise, as soon as I can, we will share more details with you.

We are thrilled to share that we are in development on a new animated series for Diablo with Netflix. pic.twitter.com/F7dKh73f12

— Diablo (@Diablo) September 12, 2026

Heroes of the Storm gets a new character

Blizzard's MOBA, Heroes of the Storm, is coming back in a big way with a new character, Xal'atah, later this month, and another new character is coming at some point afterwards. "Thank you for believing in this game," Faries said. "For carrying that torch. Who knows? We might even have another new hero on the way in the near future. So stay tuned, and we will see you in the Nexus."

BlizzCon 2026 kicks off with flashy cinematic running through all the big games

BlizzCon 2026 has started with a rousing cinematic that runs through all the big hitters. Johanna Faries is on-stage to call it a "special moment for all of us." This is Faries' first BlizzCon as boss of Blizzard, and it sounds like she's close to tears as she praises and thanks her staff. "There's so much going on at Blizzard right now that we couldn't even fit it into this weekend if we tried," she said, perhaps teasing further unnanounced projects.

Five minutes to go!

BlizzCon 2026 starts in five minutes. We're expecting Johanna Faries, President of Blizzard Entertainment, on-stage soon to start the Opening Ceremony. Almost there!

We're taking our seats... and some photos!

items.title: Wolverine Developer Insomniac Says Logan's Scent Trail Isn't Always on Amid 'Fart Gas' Toggle Requests
items.description: A debate over “fart gas” has emerged around PlayStation 5 exclusive Marvel’s Wolverine, with some people calling for developer Insomniac to add the ability to disable Logan’s scent trail entirely from the game.
items.author: Wesley Yin-Poole
items.content:
A debate over “fart gas” has emerged around PlayStation 5 exclusive Marvel’s Wolverine, with some people calling for developer Insomniac to add the ability to disable Logan’s scent trail entirely from the game.

Marvel’s Wolverine will show a scent trail for Logan to follow in certain circumstances, which had been revealed and already discussed earlier this summer. The debate around this was rekindled following the publication of Marvel’s Wolverine reviews online this week, with The Washington Post journalist Gene Park calling the scent trail “fart gas” because of the way it appears behind characters Logan follows.

Jean Grey’s fart gas trail is NOT part of the navigation assist option. i turned it on and there’s another green line that tells you where to go. mission waypoint (yellow marker) is on as well and THAT can be turned off.

2nd pic i turn off the options and the gas stays. it seems… https://t.co/XSBsGa6Xj0 pic.twitter.com/cKs9uTPSG0

— Gene Park (@GenePark) September 10, 2026

There was some confusion online about the ability to turn this feature off via accessibility options. Insomniac’s official list of accessibility options for Wolverine includes a “Chase Assist,” which lets you toggle reduced movement speed for targets during chase sequences, but it does not turn off the trail. Other navigation toggles do not turn off the scent trail either.

This has in turn led some to believe the scent trail is always on in-game, and so have called on Insomniac to add in the ability to turn it off. But Insomniac’s director of community and marketing, James Stevenson, took to social media to nip that suggestion in the bud.

“The scent trail isn’t always on,” he clarified. “It represents Logan’s canon mutant super senses and elite tracking ability. It only is there when he’s tracking a specific scent / sound (a person, whisky, or another clue scent) - story/mission moments or when he catches whiff of a collectible.”

Despite this, some still want to get rid of the “fart gas” entirely. The criticism here is that the scent trail holds the player’s hand too strongly. Referencing previous discourse about Final Fantasy’s yellow paint guides, some have said these lines remove any potential skill required for a chase sequence, for example, or exploration.

This in turn has sparked questions about the difficulty of adapting Wolverine for a video game. Given his canon mutant powers, Logan probably wouldn’t spend much time wandering through levels looking for his target — or his next drink — but that doesn’t make for particularly exciting gameplay.

Some have suggested that Logan’s scent power could be something the player can trigger with a press of R3 on the DualSense, so there’s a way for players to avoid using it if they feel that strongly about it. Based on Stevenson’s post, Insomniac didn’t feel that would make sense for Logan.

Stevenson later clarified that when it comes to finding a hidden collectible, first you have to get close enough to it to pick up the sound or scent. So, there still is a degree of exploration to be done to find them.

IGN’s Marvel’s Wolverine review returned a 6/10. We said: “Marvel's Wolverine's slick and satisfying combat wears thin well before its conclusion, so much so that even its strong character work can't quite save it from being anything more than okay.”

items.title: GTA 6 Reviews Plague Real-Life Nudist Resort After Fans Draw Comparisons to Leaks
items.description: GTA 6 fans believe its nudist resort was inspired by a real-life location, and its owners are already being bombarded with problematic reviews.
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto 6 fans believe its nudist resort was inspired by a real-life location, and its owners are already being bombarded with problematic reviews.

As if there was ever any doubt, GTA 6 fans are all over Rockstar Games' new video game. They've measured oxygen levels in hopes of predicting big reveals, showed up for Netflix announcements, and now, they've discovered what they believe was the inspiration for one of the many locations they'll visit in-game this November: Kissimmee, Florida's Cypress Cove Nudist Resort (via GamesRadar).

Fans tracking down the locations behind some of their favorite video game levels is nothing new; Arc Raiders fans did something similar in January. But where the sleuthing for some games has often resulted in real-world positivity, Cypress Cove Nudist Resort isn't enjoying the increased visibility brought by GTA 6.

"For anyone wondering about the suddenly recurring references to 'Jason Duval,' 'Lucia,' binoculars, a pool, firearms, and other suspiciously similar details — those are references to Grand Theft Auto VI," the site owner said in response to just one of the many reviews that have shown up on the Cypress Cove Nudist Resort Google page recently. "Yes. A video game."

The owner, which has already taken what action it can against the reviews, said the influx of reviews is a "coordinated series of fabricated posts using GTA VI references." They then allege that some posts were followed by requests that the rest "pay money to have the reviews changed or removed."

Their message continued, stating, "we will not pay" and "we will not negotiate," confirming it had "documented the reviews and the request for payment." It added, "This activity is being reported through the appropriate channels."

"For our actual guests and anyone researching Cypress Cove: please understand that these posts do not describe genuine guest experiences at our resort," the Cypress Cove Nudist Resort's Google representative said. "And to whoever is behind them: We appreciate the commitment to the GTA storyline, but Cypress Cove is located in Florida — not Leonida."

GTA 6 fans first caught wind of an in-game nudist resort not from Rockstar but from leaks that polluted the internet last month. Despite the lack of an official showing, early footage provided enough information for watchers to piece together how the developer might have pulled from the real world for its upgraded version of Vice City.

Whether this is the location Rockstar looked to or not, it seems that, for the most part, GTA 6-related reviews have been scrubbed from the Google page, but the site owner's message can still be found on a few of the more suspicious messages. These include references to leaks, such as a man who "pulled out his binoculars." One posted yesterday directly referenced GTA 6, saying, "Will be trying to book a reservation on Nov. 19th. I will be playing GTA 6 for three days straight while nude in my RV. Shout out to Rockstar for showing me this gem of a place!"

November 19 is, of course, the long-awaited release date for the new Grand Theft Auto game. The 13-year wait has led to lots of excitement, for better or worse, as players prepare to pick it up on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. GTA 6 fans were also able to track down the location they suspect inspired Jason and Lucia's apartment, although it is safe from any kind of review bombing.
